cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: 1.125 decimal converts to 1.02, read as 1 and 2/16
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 1.02. 0.125 * 16 = 2 sixteenths, written in the fractional notation as .02

cases.description: Documented example: the same decimal in thirty-seconds is 1.04, read as 1 and 4/32
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 1.04. 0.125 * 32 = 4 thirty-seconds, written as .04

cases.description: DOLLARFR is documented as the inverse of DOLLARDE, so a round trip returns the original notation
cases.expected_note: DOLLARDE(1.02,16) = 1.125 and DOLLARFR(1.125,16) = 1.02, so the composition is the identity on this value

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: a non-integer fraction is documented as truncated to an integer
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'If fraction is not an integer, it is truncated.' 16.9 truncates to 16, so the answer must match the first documented example, 1.02

cases.description: A fraction denominator of zero is a division by zero
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'If fraction is 0, DOLLARFR returns the #DIV/0! error value.' The DOLLARDE page words the same condition as the wider band 0 <= fraction < 1; because fraction is truncated first the two are equivalent, but the published wording differs between the pages

cases.description: A negative fraction denominator is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if fraction is less than 0
